Detailed method

The calculator opens at 500 g flour, 78% hydration, 2.5% salt, and 0.5% yeast. Oil for the pan is extra and is not in the gram total. The dough should look like a flat sheet, not a tall loaf. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir the flour, water, salt, and yeast until no dry flour remains. At 78% hydration it is sticky and slack. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Folds Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 2 to 3 hours. Give it three stretch-and-folds in the first 90 minutes, about 30 minutes apart. It should turn bubbly and jiggle.
  3. Pan Oil a rimmed sheet or a roasting pan generously. Tip the dough in. Do not drag it to the corners yet.
  4. Stretch After 20 minutes, oil your fingers and ease the dough toward the corners. If it springs back, wait another 10 minutes and finish the stretch.
  5. Proof Leave it in the pan, covered, for 45 to 75 minutes at about 24°C (75°F), until it is puffy and full of bubbles. The 0.5% yeast needs that time.
  6. Dimple Oil your fingers again and press them straight down to the pan, all over the surface. The dimples should stay open. The 2.5% salt is already in the dough.
  7. Bake Bake at 230°C (450°F) for 20 to 25 minutes, until the raised parts are deep gold and the bottom is crisp.
  8. Cool Leave it in the pan for 10 minutes, then move it to a rack. Cut it while it is warm, after the steam has eased.
